title: AI for Math Fund expands to $35.1m as new grants back open tools, theorem proving and AI-generated proofs
key_facts: Renaissance Philanthropy and XTX Markets committed a further $17.1 million to the AI for Math Fund, taking total pledged funding to $35.1 million.
The 2026 Core Grants round was first expected to give $10.5 million; organisers expanded it after more than 470 applications.
Twenty-two proposals from 30 organisations were selected, with grants of $100,000 to $1 million, running 12 to 24 months.
Projects cover AI-assisted theorem proving (AI helping construct or verify mathematical arguments), datasets, evaluation tools and research infrastructure.
The funded portfolio includes a new research pod at the Simons Institute focused on AI for mathematics and theoretical computer science.
XTX Markets and its founder Alex Gerko have committed more than $35 million to other formal mathematics initiatives, including Mathlib and the Lean Focused Research Organization.
quote_evidence: the open development of tools, training and community to accelerate AI-powered discovery in mathematics.
XTX Markets' investments have transformed formal mathematics and created a roadmap for other disciplines and funders to follow.
The challenge is not only whether a model can generate a convincing answer, but whether researchers can inspect it, verify it and build on it.
why_it_matters_hint: More money goes to open tools that let mathematicians check AI-made proofs, not only to AI that gives answers.
